title: How Much Does a Website Cost in Kenya? (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Kenyan businesses pay between KES 15,000 and KES 1.5 million for a website. Here is what each price range actually buys, and how to budget without overpaying.
author: Noon Studio Africa

content.text: If you are a business owner in Nairobi trying to figure out what a website costs in Kenya, you have probably seen quotes from KES 15,000 to KES 3 million. That range is so wide it is useless on its own.

The real answer: a professional, custom website for a Kenyan SME costs between KES 120,000 and KES 500,000, and a full e-commerce platform runs from KES 400,000 upward. What you pay depends on what you are actually buying.

This guide breaks down every price tier in plain numbers, explains what you are really paying for, and shows you how to avoid the two most expensive mistakes Kenyan businesses make. By the end, you will know exactly what to budget and what questions to ask any web design company in Kenya.

items: A template or DIY site costs KES 15,000-60,000 but rarely generates leads or ranks on Google.
A professional custom site for a Kenyan SME costs KES 120,000-500,000.
E-commerce and web applications start at KES 400,000 and take 2-4 months to build.
Ongoing costs like hosting, domain, and maintenance add KES 30,000-120,000 per year.
The cheapest option often costs more in the long run because you rebuild within a year.

content.text: The Three Tiers of Websites in Kenya
Almost every quote you receive will fall into one of three tiers. Knowing which tier you are being sold is the first step to pricing a website fairly.

rows: Pre-built template, stock images, basic hosting
Proof of concept, very early stage, digital business card
Custom design, SEO foundation, analytics, CMS, support
SMEs that need leads and rankings
Full store, payments, inventory, user accounts, 2-4 months build

content.text: 1. DIY or Template: KES 15,000-60,000
This is the Wix, GoDaddy, or cheap-freelancer route. You get a pre-built template, stock images, and basic hosting for a year. It is fine if you only need an online business card that says you exist.
Good for: sole proprietors, proof of concept, temporary landing pages. Not good for: businesses that need to compete, rank on Google, or convert visitors into paying customers.

The problem with this tier is not the price. It is the ceiling. Template sites load slowly, look like every other business on the street, and give you almost no control over search visibility. We have seen dozens of Nairobi businesses pay KES 30,000 for a template, wait six months for leads, then come back for a real build.
2. Professional Custom Build: KES 120,000-500,000

This is the tier most serious Nairobi businesses should budget for. A professionally designed and developed website built around your brand and your customers. You get custom layouts, performance optimization, an SEO foundation, analytics setup, and a content management system you can actually use without calling the developer.

items: Custom design, not a template
Responsive on phones, tablets, and desktop
Basic SEO setup: structure, meta tags, sitemap
Analytics and contact form integration
30-60 days of post-launch support
Training so your team can update content

content.text: 3. Platform or E-Commerce: KES 400,000-1.5M+

A full e-commerce platform, membership site, or custom web application lives here. Product catalogs, M-Pesa and card payment integration, inventory management, user accounts, the whole stack. These projects take 2-4 months and need ongoing maintenance, because a store is never really finished.
What You Are Really Paying For
A website quote covers far more than 'making a site'. When a studio quotes KES 320,000 for a 10-15 page site, you are buying all of the following:

items: Strategy: understanding your audience, goals, and competitive landscape
Design: layout, typography, color, and imagery that reflect your brand
Development: code that works across browsers and devices
Content: copywriting, photography, or illustration
Testing: checking forms, payments, and speed before launch
Ongoing support: fixes, updates, and optimization after launch

content.text: When a freelancer quotes KES 30,000, they are selling a template and hoping you do not ask for revisions. The difference is not the number of pages. It is who does the work and what happens after launch.
"The bitterness of poor quality remains long after the sweetness of low price is forgotten." Benjamin Franklin
The Hidden Costs Most Quotes Leave Out
The design fee is only part of the picture. A website is a running cost, not a one-time purchase. Budget for these from day one:

items: Domain name: KES 1,500-4,000 per year for a .co.ke or .com
Hosting: KES 1,000-8,000 per month depending on traffic
SSL certificate: usually included, KES 3,000-10,000 if separate
Maintenance and updates: KES 2,000-10,000 per month
Content updates: new pages, blog posts, product listings
Marketing tools: analytics, email, and booking integrations

content.text: A realistic annual budget for a professional site is the build cost plus 10-25% of that cost every year. A KES 300,000 site should carry about KES 30,000-75,000 per year in running costs. Businesses that skip maintenance usually end up with a slow, broken, or hacked site within two years.
Why Nairobi Businesses Overpay or Under-Invest
Two mistakes dominate the Kenyan market. We see both every month.

items: Under-investing: businesses pick the cheapest option, then spend six months frustrated that the site does not generate leads. They rebuild within the year, spending more in total than a proper build would have cost. A KES 35,000 template that fails and gets replaced by a KES 350,000 build is a KES 385,000 website.

Overpaying: businesses go to a large agency with big overheads, account managers, and sales commissions. The work is not necessarily better. You are paying for the sales process. A boutique studio sits in the middle: experienced people doing the work directly, without the account management theatre.

content.text: The Real Number to Budget

For most Nairobi SMEs that need a website to generate business: budget KES 200,000-500,000 for a solid custom site. That range buys a professional outcome, a partner who cares about results, and a site that earns its keep instead of sitting there as a digital brochure nobody visits.

If you are a startup with no revenue yet, the template route is an acceptable first step. Just know it is a placeholder, not a strategy. Plan the real build for the moment you have customers to serve.
How to Compare Quotes Like a Pro
When three companies quote you KES 80,000, KES 250,000, and KES 600,000 for the same project, do not pick the middle one by default. Ask every candidate the same five questions:

items: Is this a custom design or a template? Ask to see the actual design process.
Who does the work? A senior designer and developer, or a junior with a manager on top?
What happens after launch? How many months of support are included?
Is SEO included, or is it a paid extra?
Can you show me two live sites you built for businesses like mine?

content.text: The answers tell you more than the price ever will. A KES 250,000 quote from someone who shows you relevant, working case studies is usually the best deal in the room.
FAQ

items.q: How much does a simple website cost in Kenya?
items.a: A simple template or DIY website costs KES 15,000-60,000 in Kenya. A simple custom site with 3-5 pages starts around KES 120,000. The template route is cheaper upfront but rarely generates leads.

items.q: How much does it cost to maintain a website in Kenya per year?
items.a: Plan for 10-25% of the build cost per year. A KES 300,000 site needs roughly KES 30,000-75,000 annually for hosting, domain, updates, and maintenance.

items.q: Why are websites expensive in Kenya?
items.a: A serious website includes strategy, custom design, development, content, testing, and post-launch support. Cheap quotes usually cover only a template. You are paying for work that actually generates customers, not for the pages themselves.

items.q: Can I get a good website for KES 50,000 in Kenya?
items.a: You can get a decent template-based site for KES 50,000, but not a custom, SEO-ready, lead-generating website. That work realistically starts around KES 120,000 in the Kenyan market.

items.q: Do Kenyan businesses really need a website in 2026?
items.a: Yes. Customers check Google before they buy, and a website is your credibility layer. A business without one loses to competitors who show up in search results with a professional site.

content.text: Build a Website That Pays for Itself

The right number to budget is not the cheapest number. It is the number that buys a site which brings in more than it costs. For most Nairobi SMEs, that is a KES 200,000-500,000 custom build with real SEO foundations and a team that stays around after launch.
